| f-006 | defect | MAJOR | The new session-level advisory lock unlocks ordinary closure returns, including `Result::Err`, but it is not safe under panic or future cancellation. Both bypass the explicit `pg_advisory_unlock`. SQLx 0.8.6 returns `PoolConnection` to the pool on Drop unless `close_on_drop` was set, so the PostgreSQL session — and its advisory lock — survive. Reacquiring that same session is re-entrant and one later unlock leaves the leaked hold behind; another session blocks. | f-009 | defect | MAJOR | Lock contention now completes the losing ingest job successfully without reading the file. The comment's premise that the winner is reading the same bytes is false for a live-growing session: the winner can read through offset N, new bytes can arrive while it still holds the lock, and a later explicit ingest can fail `pg_try_advisory_lock`, return `Ok(None)`, and be marked done. The winner commits N; the later job that could have read N+delta has disappeared, and no future poll is guaranteed for this pull-based feature. This narrows F-006 by replacing deadlock with silent deferral/loss of the request. Smallest fix: represent contention as retry/park, or deterministically enqueue one canonical follow-up after the holder releases; do not settle the job as success.
